title: The Condition of the Working Class in England
author: Friedrich Engels
desc: Investigación de campo sobre la miseria obrera en Manchester. Documento fundacional del análisis de clase.
tesis: Engels tenía 24 años cuando recorrió los barrios obreros de Manchester y documentó lo que vio: familias hacinadas en sótanos inundados, niños trabajando 14 horas en fábricas, agua contaminada, esperanza de vida de 17 años en los barrios pobres. No es un texto teórico sino un reportaje de campo que convirtió a Engels al comunismo y anticipó los análisis de El Capital en 20 años. La miseria obrera no era un 'efecto colateral' de la industrialización sino su condición necesaria.
ideas: La miseria obrera en Manchester era sistemática y funcional: la pobreza de los trabajadores producía la riqueza de los industriales.
Engels hizo trabajo de campo en los barrios obreros — caminó las calles, habló con las familias, verificó las estadísticas.
La condición de la clase obrera inglesa en 1845 anticipa el análisis de El Capital: explotación, alienación, acumulación de capital sobre cuerpos rotos.
contexto: Engels tenía 24 años y era hijo de un industrial textil alemán con fábricas en Manchester. Llegó a Inglaterra en 1842 como empleado de la firma de su padre y se dedicó a recorrer los barrios obreros. Su compañera Mary Burns, obrera irlandesa de Manchester, fue su guía por los slums. El libro se publicó en 1845 en alemán; Marx lo leyó y fue decisivo para su colaboración.

conexiones.razon: La Condición (1845) es el reportaje empírico; El Capital (1867) es la teoría que explica por qué ocurre.
Engels documentó la miseria obrera en Inglaterra; Zinn documenta la de Estados Unidos.

quotes.text: The condition of the working-class is the real basis and point of departure of all social movements of the present because it is the highest and most unconcealed pinnacle of the social misery existing in our day.

tl: Hargreaves inventa la spinning jenny

The first invention which gave rise to a radical change in the state of the English workers was the jenny, invented in the year 1764 by a weaver, James Hargreaves, of Stanhill, near Blackburn, in North Lancashire.
Watt inventa la maquina de vapor

all this machinery was made doubly important by James Watt's steam-engine, invented in 1764 and used for supplying motive power for spinning since 1785. With these inventions, the victory of machine-work over hand-work was won.
Arkwright patenta el throstle

the factory system received a fresh extension in 1767, through the spinning throstle invented by Richard Arkwright, a barber, in Preston, in North Lancashire. After the steam-engine, this is the most important mechanical invention.
Crompton perfecciona la mule

By the combination of the peculiarities of the jenny and throstle, Samuel Crompton, of Firwood, Lancashire, contrived the mule in 1785, and as Arkwright invented the carding engine, the factory system became the prevailing one.
Ley de Aprendices del Parlamento

As early as 1796, the public objection to this revolting system found such vigorous expression through Dr. Percival and Sir Robert Peel, that in 1802 Parliament passed an Apprentices' Bill, by which the most crying evils were removed.
Aprobacion de las Corn Laws

In 1815, in order to keep up prices, the Corn Laws were passed, prohibiting the importation of corn so long as the price of wheat continued less than 80 shillings per quarter. These laws did not ameliorate the distress.
Owen agita desde New Lanark

Later, towards 1817, Robert Owen, then a manufacturer in New Lanark, in Scotland, afterwards founder of English Socialism, began to call the attention of the Government, by memorials and petitions, to the necessity of legislative guarantees.
Huelga general de los mineros escoceses

So, too, in 1818, the association of Scottish miners was powerful enough to carry on a general strike. These associations required their members to take an oath of fidelity and secrecy, had regular lists, treasurers, book-keepers, and local branches.
Primera Factory Act, papel mojado

The late Sir Robert Peel and other philanthropists united with him, and gradually secured the Factory Acts of 1819, 1825, and 1831, of which the first two were never enforced, and the last only here and there.
Se revocan las Combination Acts

This was enacted in 1824, and repealed all laws by which coalitions between working-men for labour purposes had hitherto been forbidden. The working-men obtained a right previously restricted to the aristocracy and bourgeoisie, the right of free association.
Se revocan las Combination Acts
When, on the other hand, the working-men received in 1824 the right of free association, these combinations were very soon spread over all England and attained great power.
Comienza el ciclo de crisis industriales

This was the period apparently indicated by the course of events from 1825 to 1842. The numbers of arrests for criminal offences reached: 1825, 14,457; 1830, 18,107; 1835, 20,731; 1840, 27,187; 1842, 31,309 in England and Wales alone.
Ferrocarril Liverpool-Manchester
The first great one was opened from Liverpool to Manchester in 1830, since which all the great cities have been connected by rail.
Reform Bill amplía sufragio a la burguesía
The first electoral reform bill was introduced in Parliament in March 1831 and adopted in June 1832. It put an end to the political monopoly of the landed aristocracy, bankers and usurers.
Reform Bill amplía sufragio a la burguesía

the law of 1832 fixed high property qualifications in the towns (10 pounds) and counties (50 pounds), thus first opening the doors of Parliament only to representatives of the industrial bourgeoisie. The proletariat and the petty bourgeoisie remained disfranchised.
Reform Bill amplía sufragio a la burguesía

The Reform Bill of 1831 had been the victory of the whole capitalist class over the landed aristocracy. The Reform Bill had legally sanctioned the distinction between bourgeoisie and proletariat, and made the bourgeoisie the ruling class.
Factory Act y comision investigadora

The Report of the Factories' Inquiry Commission of 1833 relates that the manufacturers began to employ children rarely of five years, often of six, very often of seven; that the working-day often lasted fourteen to sixteen hours.
Factory Act y comision investigadora

The result of this report was the Factory Act of 1833, which forbade the employment of children under nine years of age (except in silk mills), limited the working-hours of children between 9-13 years to 48 per week, or 9 hours in any one day at the utmost; that of young persons from 14-18 years of age to 69 per week, or 12 on any one day as the maximum, provided for an hour and a half as the minimum interval for meals, and repeated the total prohibition of night-work for persons under eighteen years of age.
New Poor Law y las Bastillas de los pobres

They accordingly brought in the New Poor Law, which was passed by Parliament in 1834... All relief in money and provisions was abolished; the only relief allowed was admission to the workhouses immediately built. The regulations for these workhouses, or, as the people call them, Poor Law Bastilles, is such as to frighten away every one who has the slightest prospect of life without this form of public charity.
New Poor Law y las Bastillas de los pobres

To make sure that relief be applied for only in the most extreme cases and after every other effort had failed, the workhouse has been made the most repulsive residence which the refined ingenuity of a Malthusian can invent.
Nueva Poor Law y proletarizacion del campo

the modification of the Poor Law was the first measure which the State was obliged to apply to the daily increasing impoverishment of the country parishes; the working-class commands two-thirds less subsistence than from 1834-1836.
Lovett redacta la People's Charter

In 1838 a committee of the General Working-men's Association of London, with William Lovett at its head, drew up the People's Charter, whose six points are: Universal suffrage for every man who is of age, Annual Parliaments, Payment of members.
Kersall Moor: cuestión de cuchillo y tenedor

Chartism, my friends, is no political movement, where the main point is your getting the ballot. Chartism is a knife and fork question: the Charter means a good house, good food and drink, prosperity, and short working-hours.
Old Town de Manchester y el río Irk

At the bottom flows, or rather stagnates, the Irk, a narrow, coal-black, foul-smelling stream, full of debris and refuse... bubbles of miasmatic gas constantly arise and give forth a stench unendurable even on the bridge forty or fifty feet above the surface of the stream.
Old Town de Manchester y el río Irk

such a district exists in the heart of the second city of England, the first manufacturing city of the world. If any one wishes to see in how little space a human being can move, how little air — and such air! — he can breathe, how little of civilisation he may share and yet live, it is only necessary to travel hither.
Insurrecciones cartistas en el Norte y Gales

In 1839 Bussey, Taylor, and Frost hastened to call forth uprisings simultaneously in the North of England, in Yorkshire, and Wales. Frost's plan being betrayed, he was obliged to open hostilities prematurely.
Insurrecciones cartistas en el Norte y Gales

In 1839 the agitation continued as vigorously as ever, and when it began to relax somewhat at the end of the year, Bussey, Taylor, and Frost hastened to call forth uprisings simultaneously in the North of England, in Yorkshire, and Wales. Frost's plan being betrayed, he was obliged to open hostilities prematurely.
Crisis, peticion cartista y alianza con liberales

The crisis of 1842 came on. The year's national petition for the Charter with its three and a half million signatures proves. At a meeting of Liberals and Chartists held in Manchester, February 14th, 1842, a petition was drawn up.
Plug Plot: huelga general del norte

August 8th they proceeded to Ashton and Hyde five thousand strong, closed all the mills and coal-pits, and held meetings, in which, however, the question discussed was not, as the bourgeoisie had hoped, the repeal of the Corn Laws, but, 'a fair day's wages for a fair day's work.'
Plug Plot: huelga general del norte

August 9th they proceeded to Manchester, unresisted by the authorities (all Liberals), and closed the mills; on the 11th they were in Stockport, where they met with the first resistance as they were storming the workhouse, the favourite child of the bourgeoisie.
Crisis comercial y Liga Anti-Corn Law
When I came to Manchester in November, 1842, there were crowds of unemployed working-men at every street corner, and many mills were still standing idle.
Atentado contra la fabrica de Ainsworth y Crompton

On Friday, October 6th, 1843, an attempt to set fire to the factory of Ainsworth and Crompton, at Bolton, did no damage; it was the third or fourth attempt in the same factory within a very short time.
Lord Ashley y la jornada de diez horas

on March 19th, 1844, Lord Ashley carried, with a majority of 179 to 170, a resolution that the word 'Night' in the Factory Act should express the time from six at night to six in the morning, whereby the prohibition of night-work came to mean the limitation of working-hours to twelve, including free hours, or ten hours of actual work a day.
Engels escribe el libro en Manchester

The book was first issued in Germany in 1845. The author, at that time, was young, twenty-four years of age. Whole districts which in 1844 I could describe as almost idyllic have now fallen into dilapidation.
Londres como guerra social abierta
The brutal indifference, the unfeeling isolation of each in his private interest, becomes the more repellent and offensive, the more these individuals are crowded together, within a limited space.
Londres como guerra social abierta
Hence it comes, too, that the social war, the war of each against all, is here openly declared.
